title: CPP-SGS: Cycle-Accurate Power Prediction Framework via SNN and Genetic Signal Selection
problem: Accurate cycle-by-cycle power prediction requires monitoring numerous signals; traditional approaches face scalability and computational overhead issues in runtime power management.
motivation: Runtime power management is critical for IC performance and longevity; cycle-accurate prediction enables dynamic optimization but requires efficient signal selection.
method: The method uses Genetic Algorithms (a search technique that mimics evolution) to identify which signals flowing through a chip matter most for power prediction, then feeds only those key signals into Spiking Neural Networks (neural networks modeled on how neurons fire in bursts, which efficiently learn patterns over time). By reducing the number of signals needed, the model becomes smaller and faster to run, enabling real-time power management.
key_novelty: The core idea is combining Genetic Algorithms for signal selection with Spiking Neural Networks—neural networks that efficiently handle time-series patterns by processing discrete events—to achieve a compact, accurate model for predicting power consumption.
contributions: Cycle-accurate power prediction framework combining SNNs and GAs
Reduced model size and inference latency via genetic signal selection
limitations: Baseline comparison details and scalability to different chip architectures not discussed.
primary_theme: SNN-based cycle-accurate power prediction with GA feature selection
